articles.title: WHO warns ‘more complex’ Ebola outbreak now present in 3 African countries
Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa

events.summary: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case as an outbreak spread across three African countries. Health officials are actively investigating the source of the infection.
events.why: The entry of Ebola into densely populated West African nations poses a catastrophic regional public health threat.

articles.title: WHO supports Nigeria after first Ebola case confirmed

events.summary: The WHO has deployed assistance to Nigeria following the country's first confirmed case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease.
events.why: The arrival of a lethal Ebola strain in Africa's most populous nation requires urgent international containment to prevent a major epidemic.

articles.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back

events.summary: Global temperatures are projected to exceed the 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels. Rapid and deep emissions cuts are required to minimize the overshoot and bring warming back within agreed targets by century's end.
events.why: Breaching 1.5°C drives irreversible climate tipping points and accelerates global environmental instability.

articles.title: DR Congo: Ebola responders under pressure as outbreak expands

events.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to an eighth province. Investigators are actively pursuing leads to assess the risk of transmission into Nigeria.
events.why: Expansion of a deadly infectious disease across provinces and potentially between nations creates severe public health and containment challenges.

articles.title: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis

events.summary: Nearly two dozen countries met in Geneva to advance peace efforts aimed at halting the conflict and drone warfare in Sudan. The talks seek to establish a ceasefire and a transition to representative governance to relieve the humanitarian crisis.
events.why: Diplomatic efforts are critical to halting an intense conflict and deep humanitarian emergency affecting millions of Sudanese citizens.

articles.title: UN agencies appeal for help to protect weakest from unprecedented El Niño

events.summary: Two UN agencies have appealed for urgent international aid to protect vulnerable communities from the strongest recorded El Niño pattern. The weather event is already causing severe impacts across multiple regions.
events.why: Record extreme weather events threaten food security, infrastructure, and survival for millions globally.

articles.title: M 7.0 - 191 km ENE of Nagqu, China

events.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck east-northeast of Nagqu, China, at a depth of 18 km. The event triggered an Orange PAGER alert and a ShakeMap intensity of VIII.
events.why: A shallow magnitude 7.0 earthquake with an orange alert indicates significant ground shaking and risk of regional destruction.

articles.title: Why a student protest movement is challenging 12 years of Vučić rule in Serbia
Thousands gather at final student-led rally ahead of Serbia election

events.summary: Serbians are voting in elections following two years of student-led protests against the ruling party. The vote follows a final major rally and could alter 12 years of rule under President Vučić.
events.why: National elections could potentially shift state governance and foreign alignment in a key Balkan nation.

articles.title: World News in Brief: Aid for Ethiopia, Abyei drone strikes condemned, extreme heat and newborn health

events.summary: The WHO is expanding emergency health operations across Ethiopia's Afar, Amhara, and Tigray regions. The scale-up aims to meet rising humanitarian and medical needs caused by continued hostilities.
events.why: Emergency medical aid is essential to sustaining civilians in regions crippled by armed conflict.

articles.title: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes

events.summary: A report by UNODC and IOM revealed that migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees along European sea routes last year. The finding highlights the massive financial scale of illicit maritime trafficking networks.
events.why: Illicit revenues in the hundreds of millions fuel international criminal networks and exploit vulnerable populations.

articles.title: ‘Ominous start’ to West Bank olive harvest amid settler attacks

events.summary: Settler attacks involving live ammunition, arson, and the destruction of centuries-old olive trees have disrupted the West Bank harvest. The incidents have severely affected the opening weeks of the seasonal harvest.
events.why: Attacks directly destroy generational agricultural livelihoods and escalate territorial instability in the West Bank.

articles.title: Fate unknown of many returned to DPR Korea from China: UN independent experts

events.summary: UN independent experts reported ongoing concerns regarding the unknown fate of North Korean nationals forcibly returned from China. Large-scale forcible repatriations resumed three years ago according to the report.
events.why: Forced repatriations place returnees at grave risk of severe human rights abuses and detention.

articles.title: North Korea says it will resume propaganda broadcasts across border into South Korea
North Korea prepares to restart propaganda loudspeakers as ties sour with South

events.summary: North Korea announced plans to resume psychological warfare broadcasts using loudspeakers along its border with South Korea. The decision was confirmed by leader Kim Jong Un's sister amid deteriorating inter-Korean relations.
events.why: Resumption of border psychological warfare marks rising military friction on the Korean Peninsula.
